enumeration_method: Surface A (documentation, 993 items): Read the Docs' own sitemap.xml lists every public build of the project (18 builds: develop, latest, stable, 2026.2, 2026.1, 2025.12, 2025.5, 2025.1.3, 2024.10, 2024.8.1, 2024.8, 2024.7, 2024.4, 4.9.0, 4.8.0, 4.7.0, 4.4.0, 4.3.0). Each Sphinx build ships its own searchindex.js, whose `docnames` array is that build's complete document set - the catalogue's own index, not a nav-tree sample. `stable` resolves to the same 395-docname build as `latest`, so it is an alias and not a second population. The English tree exists only for `latest`: every other /en/<build>/ root returns 404 (checked 2026-09-24), so all 395 English docnames are judged at /en/latest/. The Russian union across the 17 distinct builds is 598 docnames; each is judged once, at the newest build that still contains it (203 docnames exist only in older builds and are fetched there). No keyword facet was used; nothing was filtered before judgement. Surface B (repository, 1 item): the ecos-demo-app tree was enumerated in full through the GitHub trees API (83 entries, truncated=false) and contains exactly one BPMN artefact, src/main/resources/eapps/artifacts/process/bpmn/demo-process.bpmn.xml; the other 82 entries are Java sources, YAML model definitions, Docker/compose files and READMEs, none of which is a process drawing.
note: How the 994 items were judged. Every one of the 993 documentation URLs was fetched (993/993 HTTP 200) and its main text, figure inventory, figure file names, the section heading that precedes each figure, and every .bpmn/.bar link target were extracted from the page itself; the repository item was read through the GitHub API. No item was judged from a URL slug or a search snippet. Evidence channels, in the order of weight. (1) Downloadable BPMN XML - complete: the whole population carries exactly four .bpmn files on six pages (en 348/356/365 and their ru builds 940/948/957). All four were downloaded and parsed: two carry the platform AI task (aiTask, aiUserInput, aiPreprocessingScript, aiPostprocessingScript, aiAddDocumentToContext, aiSaveResultToDocument, aiResponse) and are recorded at 001; the other two (test-bpmn-process, assignee-changed-listener-example) contain no AI attribute and are dismissed by E2 on rows 356/948 and 365/957. (2) Page text and DOM - complete: the AI/LLM keyword population is 40 pages (33 in the review band plus their ru builds), every one of them was read and its AI sentence judged by hand; that is where the E2 dismissals name the AI mention they dismiss (an assistant, a semantic-search service, a config key, a navigation entry, AI that generates the diagram). (3) Rendered figures - the AI-and-BPMN facet (every page under settings_kb/processes/**, the AI sections, and every page whose figure is named after a drawing or an AI thing): 781 figures were downloaded and 701 distinct contents found (80 files are byte-identical re-publications across the en/ru trees, which is the evidence behind the two E3 rows); the AI Task page, the components catalogue, the designer page (369) and the BPMN_ecos page (336) were inspected at native resolution - the designer's canvases carry the BPMN.IO watermark and show status/user tasks with the AI element present only in the palette and the assistant button, which is why 369 and 336 are E2 and not records. Recorded limitation (open gap). Read the Docs answered HTTP 429 to the later figure bursts, so the remaining ~535 diagram figures of the non-AI pages could not be fetched; the 56 E2 rows that say 'the page draws the module business process under the heading ...' and the 7 E1 rows therefore rest on the page's own heading and text rather than on a pixel-level inspection, except for the pages whose figures were fetched and viewed contact-sheet scale (bp.png on row 173 was verified as a BPMN 2.0 diagram). The residual risk is a BPMN diagram carrying an AI element on a page that never mentions AI anywhere in its text - no such page exists in this source's text (checked), so the risk is confined to an AI element drawn inside a figure whose page is silent about AI. No item was excluded for being small, foreign-language, marketing, or similar to another; the ru pages are not duplicates of the en ones except where the same downloadable process or the same 14-figure component inventory is literally shared (E3, rows 940 and 960). Three image references in the ru/develop build 404 (ru/develop/_images/*.png) - a broken reference in that build, not a blocked item. The ecos-demo-app repository holds one BPMN file and no AI element (row 994). VISUAL BACKSTOP (2026-09-25): all 765 raw figures (116 pages) were viewed on 64 contact sheets with a per-tile sidecar. The pass CONFIRMED the census's central find - the Citeck AI Task is a first-class BPMN element (a rounded task with a sparkle icon, label "AI Task"), shown end-to-end in two processes ("Комментарий сравнение версий" and "Генерация текста КП"), already recorded at rows 348/368 (EN) and deduplicated at rows 940/960 (RU mirror). It found no AI-labelled element inside any other diagram: the Russian equipment-request, offer, HR, service-desk, book-request and release processes resolved at native size all carry plain status/approval/notification vocabulary, the AI on the AI case-sample page is the assistant dock that GENERATES the diagram (tool-level, not an element in it), and the AI-agent/RAG screenshots (rows 525, 638, 940 panel shots) are configuration UI, not process models. Two figure families that look like process models are not: the Architecture-page box-and-arrow schematics (985/622/387/110) and the DMN decision tables (948_process_04, 356_process_04). Five rows whose BPMN figures could not be read at the asset's own resolution were superseded to UNCERTAIN with needs_visual_check (185, 738, 740, 930, 957). Residual doubt the researcher may want to close, left as it stands because the tiles WERE looked at and showed no AI label at sheet scale: 946_bpmn_notification_example_process.png, 948_59/60/61/62, 948_sample_011, the 956/957 start-event and sub-process example figures, 889_History_3.png, 743_desk_8/9.png, 744_tasks_1.png, and the palette of 336_0127 / 341_message_bpmn / 345_rights_3 (a palette entry is not an element inside the process in any case).
